used 500 μL of lysis buffer per 25 mg of mollusc tissue. Amount of lysis buffer per sample could be scaled down. EDTA is a metal ion chelator. By binding to Mg 2+ , DNase activity is stopped as it is dependent on Mg 2+ .

Vortex lysis and precipitation buffers, then place both in the 60°C incubator or water bath. Leave buffers at 60°C until needed at later steps. Necessary to dissolve the CTAB and may take 20 min or longer. Further vortexing or inverting may be also be required.

Quantify the DNA on a Nanodrop and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad-range assay) (both instruments from Thermo Fisher Scientific). The DNA will be somewhat crude, containing some degraded RNA and potentially residual protein or other contaminants, which will be removed later. For Nanodrop, use 1 μL. As degraded RNA may still be present, Nanodrop results may give a large over-estimation of concentration. Qubit fluorometer is the most reliable. However, it is highly dependent on the accuracy of the amount pipetted. Use 2 μL when sample is plentiful. Using 1 μL is prone to pipetting errors. For pure DNA, Nanodrop:Qubit is 1:1, 260/280 is 1.8 and 260/230 is 2.0.

Quantify the DNA on a Nanodrop and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad-range assay) (both instruments from Thermo Fisher Scientific). The DNA should be pure, free of contaminants. Expect 10-30% recovery relative to total input.

steps.title: Collect and freeze fungal material
steps.instruction: Grow the fungus, harvest approximately 500 mg of tissue or spores (e.g., rust fungi), and keep the material frozen at –80 °C or in liquid nitrogen until use; note that small‑genome fungi (~50 Mb) may require two prep rounds, while larger genomes may need fewer spores.

steps.title: Prepare chilled mortar and pestle
steps.instruction: Place a sterile mortar and pestle inside an insulated container (e.g., ice‑box lid), add liquid nitrogen to chill the tools (do not pour LN₂ directly onto the sample), and ensure the container will not crack or spill.

steps.title: Add sand and grind sample
steps.instruction: Add about 1 g of acid‑washed, autoclaved sand (up to 2 g if needed) to the chilled mortar, add the frozen fungal sample, and grind thoroughly for 2–3 min while keeping the mortar surrounded by liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Transfer to lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the ground sample and sand into a tube containing CTAB lysis buffer (ensure the tube is a 50 mL Falcon; if the mixture occupies >50 % of the tube, split into a larger tube or two tubes).

steps.title: Add RNase A and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of 20 mg mL⁻¹ RNase A stock and 150 µL of 20 mg mL⁻¹ Proteinase K stock to achieve a final concentration of 200 µg mL⁻¹ for each (recommended 50–100 µg mL⁻¹); mix by vortexing and inverting.

steps.title: Lysis incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate at 60 °C for 60–90 min in a rotating/shaking incubator (or water bath, noting lower yield); rotation or gentle shaking is preferred.

steps.title: First chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1 v/v) to the lysate, invert 10–15 times to mix, then centrifuge at 5 000 rcf for 10 min at 20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Second chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol, invert 10–15 times, and centrifuge again at 5 000 rcf for 10 min at 20 °C; transfer the aqueous phase to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Add precipitation buffer
steps.instruction: Add two volumes of precipitation buffer (e.g., 30 mL to ~15 mL of aqueous phase), swirl and invert several times to mix.

steps.title: CTAB‑DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 60 °C in a rotating/shaking incubator (≈150 rpm) for 1–2.5 h (minimum 1 h) until white CTAB‑DNA crystals are visible; note that CTAB concentration in the lysis buffer is now 4 % w/v.

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16 000 rcf for 20 min at 20 °C (alternatively 2 × 15 min spins); a visible pellet should form.

steps.title: Decant supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant without disturbing the fragile pellet; optionally retain the supernatant in a separate tube in case DNA has not precipitated.

steps.title: Ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 10–15 mL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol (enough to cover the pellet), gently swirl and invert, then centrifuge at 16 000 rcf for 5 min.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 10–15 min (or until all ethanol has evaporated).

steps.title: CTAB salt soak
steps.instruction: Let the dried pellet soak at room temperature for 15 min to dissolve excess salts and residual CTAB.

steps.title: Temperature equilibration
steps.instruction: Briefly place the tube at room temperature or on ice to bring the temperature down.

steps.title: Hydration before resuspension
steps.instruction: Incubate the pellet at room temperature for 5–10 min to ensure complete hydration, then place the tube on ice.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Pipette 100–200 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8 (or nuclease‑free water) onto the pellet; repeatedly add the same volume and pipette gently until the pellet fully dissolves, avoiding vigorous mixing that could shear DNA.

steps.title: Transfer to LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the DNA solution to a 1.5 mL DNA LoBind Eppendorf tube and store at 4 °C to prevent freeze‑thaw‑induced shearing.

steps.title: Optional RNA‑degradation bead clean
steps.instruction: If large amounts of degraded RNA are suspected, add 1 × volume AMPure XP beads to the DNA solution, incubate 5 min at room temperature, place on a magnetic rack 5 min, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 1 mL 80 % ethanol, air‑dry 1–4 min (do not over‑dry), and elute with 50 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8 (10 min incubation).

steps.title: Size selection with PippinHT
steps.instruction: Load 20–30 µg of DNA per lane (20 µL DNA + 5 µL loading buffer) onto a PippinHT (or similar) using a 15 kb high‑pass (or 20 kb if DNA is abundant); run the instrument, then wait at least 45 min (or longer) for elution.

steps.title: Collect Pippin eluate
steps.instruction: Pool the contents of all elution wells into a 1.5 mL or 2 mL Eppendorf tube (≈250–300 µL).

steps.title: Add Tween to eluate
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL of 0.1 % Tween‑20 in electrophoresis buffer to each elution well, wait 5 min, then combine the added volume with the pooled eluate (total ≈600 µL).

steps.title: Bead‑based clean‑up
steps.instruction: Add at least 1 × volume AMPure XP beads (~600 µL) to the pooled eluate (or, if using 2 % Sera‑Mag beads, fill ~90 % of the tube capacity with binding buffer and add 100 µL beads); incubate 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Magnetic separation and ethanol washes
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack for 5 min (or until clear), discard supernatant, then while the tube remains on the magnet add 1 mL 80 % ethanol, discard, and repeat for a second ethanol wash.

steps.title: Dry beads
steps.instruction: Remove all traces of ethanol and air‑dry the beads for 1–4 min; do not let the beads dry completely.

steps.title: First bead elution
steps.instruction: Elute DNA from the beads with 50 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8 (or nuclease‑free water), incubate 10 min at room temperature, then place on a magnetic rack for 5 min and transfer the eluate to a 1.5 mL LoBind tube (maximum 48 µL for ONT ligation prep).

steps.title: Second bead elution
steps.instruction: Perform a second elution by adding another 50 µL Tris‑HCl, incubating 10 min, magnetising, and transferring the eluate to a separate 1.5 mL LoBind tube for alternative applications (e.g., PFGE or Illumina library).

steps.title: Final storage
steps.instruction: Store all purified DNA at 4 °C to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles that could shear high‑molecular‑weight DNA.

steps.title: Alternative polymer‑salt size selection
steps.instruction: If desired, perform size selection using a polymer‑and‑salt solution as described in the referenced DNA clean‑up protocol (or use a commercial kit such as the Circulomics Short‑Read Eliminator); only the size‑selection portion of that protocol is required.
